title: Given an integer array, find the contiguous subarray with the largest product and return that product.
shortTitle: Maximum Product Subarray — track max and min together

s1_definition.profdef: Linear DP that tracks both the running maximum and running minimum product ending at each index, because a negative number swaps them. At each element: newMax = max(x, x·max, x·min), newMin = min(x, x·max, x·min). Track the global maximum. Time O(n), space O(1).
s1_definition.analogy: A returns analyst at National Bank of India multiplies consecutive daily growth factors to find the best stretch. A single loss factor (a negative) can flip the biggest gain into the biggest loss and vice versa, so she keeps both the best and worst running product at every day.
s1_definition.oneliner: Keep running max AND min; a negative swaps them; answer is the global max.
s1_definition.raw:
**Professional definition:** Linear DP that tracks both the running maximum and running minimum product ending at each index, because a negative number swaps them. At each element: newMax = max(x, x·max, x·min), newMin = min(x, x·max, x·min). Track the global maximum. Time O(n), space O(1).

**In simple words (banking analogy):** A returns analyst at National Bank of India multiplies consecutive daily growth factors to find the best stretch. A single loss factor (a negative) can flip the biggest gain into the biggest loss and vice versa, so she keeps both the best and worst running product at every day.

**One line to remember:** Keep running max AND min; a negative swaps them; answer is the global max.

sections.s2_technical:
Unlike maximum sum, product has a twist: multiplying by a negative turns a large positive into a large negative and a large negative into a large positive. So you must carry both the maximum and the minimum product ending at the current index. Initialize both and the answer to the first element.

At each next element x, compute candidates x, x times the previous max, and x times the previous min, then set the new max to the largest and the new min to the smallest. For example: `int cand1 = x*max, cand2 = x*min; max = Math.max(x, Math.max(cand1, cand2)); min = Math.min(x, Math.min(cand1, cand2));`. Update the global answer with the new max. Note you must compute the new max from the OLD max and min, so capture them before overwriting.

The time is O(n) and space is O(1). A senior nuance is that zeros naturally reset both running products because x itself becomes a candidate, so the subarray effectively restarts after a zero without any special casing.
sections.s3_banking:
Problem 1 — At National Bank of India, a returns analyst multiplies consecutive daily growth factors to find the most profitable contiguous stretch of trading days. This is exactly how Maximum Product Subarray works.

Problem 2 — A single negative growth factor can flip the sign of the running product, so tracking only the maximum misses the case where a future negative turns a current minimum into the new maximum. This is exactly why both the running max and min are carried.

The mini-project builds a `ReturnsAnalyzer`, a `BankLogFormatter`, and a runnable demo.

sections.s5_journey:
The input factors are two, three, minus two, four.

Step 1: Max, min, and answer all start at two.

Step 2: At three, the max becomes six and the min becomes three, and the answer becomes six.

Step 3: At minus two, the candidates flip signs, so the new max is minus two and the new min is minus twelve, while the answer stays six.

Step 4: At four, the candidates are four, minus eight, and minus forty-eight, so the max is four and the answer stays six.

Step 5: The maximum product is six, and the second example resets at the zero and yields zero.

```text
2026-10-27T03:40:00Z [INFO] National Bank of India — Returns Analyzer (Maximum Product Subarray)
2026-10-27T03:40:00Z [INFO] Maximum product subarray = 6
2026-10-27T03:40:00Z [INFO] {2,3,-2,4} → 6
2026-10-27T03:40:00Z [INFO] Maximum product subarray = 0
2026-10-27T03:40:00Z [INFO] {-2,0,-1} → 0
```

sections.s6_takeaway:
Maximum Product Subarray is a linear dynamic programming problem with a twist compared to the maximum sum version. The twist is that multiplying by a negative number flips a large positive product into a large negative one and vice versa, so I cannot track only the running maximum. I carry both the running maximum product and the running minimum product ending at the current index.

At each element I compute three candidates: the element alone, the element times the previous maximum, and the element times the previous minimum. The new maximum is the largest of these and the new minimum is the smallest, and I always compute them from the old values before overwriting. I update a global answer with each new maximum. Zeros need no special handling because the element itself is a candidate, which naturally restarts the subarray.

In my project at National Bank of India, a returns analyst multiplied consecutive daily growth factors to find the most profitable contiguous stretch of trading days. Because one negative factor could flip the running product, I tracked both the best and the worst running product so a later negative could turn the worst into the best, and it runs in linear time with constant space.
